vectors.name: float/float64/1.5
vectors.description: Exact in half precision.

vectors.name: float/float64/1
vectors.description: Integral float value 1.0 declared float64: shortest exact width is half precision. A JavaScript sender may also send integer 0x01, which decoders MUST accept (section 3.1). Floats never appear in canonical data (section 3.2).

vectors.name: float/integer-on-wire
vectors.description: Decoders MUST accept an integer where a float type is declared (JavaScript cannot tell 3 from 3.0). The wire bytes 0x03 decode to float64 3.0; the canonical encoding of 3.0 is f94200.

vectors.name: struct/note

vectors.name: struct/note-pinned

vectors.name: map/text-keys
vectors.description: Map string => uint. Core Deterministic Encoding sorts keys by their encoded bytes, so "b" (61 62) sorts before "aa" (62 61 61): shorter strings first, unlike plain string order.

vectors.name: map/uint-keys
vectors.description: Map uint => string: 24 (18 18) sorts after 23 (17).

vectors.name: map/metadata-hub
vectors.description: Metadata with all core keys a hub sets when forwarding (section 10.6): deadline (32), context (36, bytes), principal (37, string), plus an application text key.

vectors.name: map/mixed-keys
vectors.description: A map with keys of mixed CBOR major types, as in a generic CBOR value (the CDDL `any` of an annotation value or of Error.details). These keys are not metadata symbols: -1 and -25 are not uints or text, and 1, 24 and 35 are not used as metadata keys here. Core Deterministic Encoding orders uints (major type 0) before negative ints (1) before text (3), bytewise, so 24 (18 18) sorts before -1 (20).

vectors.name: map/params
vectors.description: A params map (section 5.4) in canonical order.

vectors.name: depth/64-arrays
vectors.description: Item whose value is 63 nested arrays around the uint 1. With the message's own array as level 1, the message is nested exactly 64 levels deep and MUST be accepted; the scalar inside adds no level (3.1).

vectors.name: depth/65-arrays
vectors.description: The same Item with one more array: nested 65 levels deep, so a decoder MUST reject it (3.1).

vectors.name: depth/64-mixed
vectors.description: Item whose value alternates arrays and maps {"k": ...}, with tag 1 (an integer timestamp) as the innermost level: arrays, maps and tags all count, and the message is nested exactly 64 levels deep. Accepted (3.1).

vectors.name: depth/65-mixed
vectors.description: The same with one more level: the tag is level 65, so a decoder MUST reject the message (3.1).

vectors.name: non-shortest/credit
vectors.description: Credit [24, 6, 100] with a one-byte array length (98 03) and every integer in a longer form than needed (kind 19 00 18, call ID 1a 00000006, amount 19 0064). Senders use the shortest form; a receiver MUST accept this one as the same message (3.1).

vectors.name: non-shortest/float-width
vectors.description: Item [18, 6, 1.5] with the float sent as a 64-bit float (fb) although half precision is exact. Decoders MUST accept any float width (3.1).

vectors.name: non-shortest/text-length
vectors.description: Error [20, 2, 13, "hello", null] with the text length written as 78 05 instead of 65 (3.1).

vectors.name: non-shortest/unsorted-metadata
vectors.description: Request whose metadata lists the text key before sigil key 32. Ordinary messages need not sort map keys (3.2): this is another valid encoding of the same message.
